techniques.name: Five-layer gunshot stack (Kilborn model) replacing flat single-burst
techniques.howItWorks: Pro FPS gunshots are not one sound; they are 5 simultaneous sub-mixes time-aligned to the same trigger: (1) TRANSIENT — the <5ms attack click that gives the ear its 'is it close/loud' cue; (2) BODY — the broadband 1-4kHz report that carries weapon identity; (3) SUB/LFE — a 30-120Hz sine thump for chest-punch; (4) MECHANICAL — the bolt/action clack 8-25ms AFTER the report; (5) TAIL — the environment decay. Each layer is independently EQ'd/decayed so they read as one event but are individually shapeable per weapon and per distance. This is the canonical AAA gunshot architecture (Mark Kilborn, Call of Duty audio director).
techniques.webAudioMapping: Per-shot: build all five as offset sub-graphs into the per-cue gain. TRANSIENT = noiseBurst(highpass 6kHz, Q0.5, dur 0.004, exponential decay). BODY = noiseBurst(bandpass center 2.5kHz, Q1.5) layered with a peaking noiseBurst at the weapon's formant. SUB = sub() sine 120->60Hz, dur 0.05. MECHANICAL = noiseBurst(bandpass ~3kHz metallic, Q4, peak 0.15) scheduled at crack+0.012..0.025. TAIL = a wet ConvolverNode send (see tail technique). The repo's noiseBurst/sub/tone primitives already exist in lib/audio/synth.ts — this is restructuring each muzzle_* case into 5 named layers, not new primitives.
techniques.source: How to Sound Design FPS Gunshots — Mark Kilborn (Pro Sound Effects) https://blog.prosoundeffects.com/how-to-sound-design-first-person-shooter-gunshot-sound-effects-with-mark-kilborn ; corroborated by Splice weapon-design guide & Springer physically-motivated model

techniques.name: True supersonic N-wave crack as a separate physical layer (not just bright noise)
techniques.howItWorks: The 'crack' is NOT the muzzle report — it is the ballistic shock wave: a Mach cone the bullet drags. Its acoustic signature is an N-wave: a near-instant pressure rise, a linear ramp-down through zero, total duration only ~150-300 microseconds for a rifle round (longer = bigger caliber, longer = greater miss distance). That sub-millisecond N-wave is why a passing round is a sharp 'snap/whipcrack' with energy biased very high (its short period maps to multi-kHz content), perceptually distinct from the lower, diffuse muzzle thump. Caliber sets the N-wave PERIOD: 7.62 (longer/heavier bullet) gives a slightly longer, lower-pitched crack than 5.56. This is the highest-leverage realism cue for incoming fire in a CO-IN sim.
techniques.webAudioMapping: Model the N-wave shape explicitly, don't approximate with filtered noise: synthesize a 0.3-0.5ms 'click' = a single short noiseBurst(highpass ~4-6kHz, Q0.3, dur 0.0004-0.0008, attack 0.00005) — the ultra-short envelope IS the N-wave period. Bias the period by caliber: 5.56 dur 0.00035 + highpass 5kHz (brighter); 7.62 dur 0.0006 + highpass 3.5kHz (woodier). Schedule it at crackAt (the speed-of-sound-corrected arrival of the round at the camera), with the muzzle report layer at thumpAt. Only fire it for rounds that pass NEAR the listener (the repo's nearmiss cue is the seam — upgrade its bandpass-0.02s burst to this true short N-wave).
techniques.source: Crack & Thump method (Max Velocity Tactical) https://maxvelocitytactical.com/crack-thump/ ; The ballistic wave physics (HAL hal-01103309) ; CDC auditory N-wave study; Springer/Farnell shockwave model

techniques.name: Crack-thump speed-of-sound split as a ranging cue (already seeded, extend it)
techniques.howItWorks: For supersonic incoming, the shock crack arrives FIRST (it travels with the bullet at >Mach 1), then the muzzle 'thump' follows at the speed of sound (~343 m/s). The gap is a learnable range cue: ~0.5s at 300m, ~1.0s at 600m, near-zero under 100m. The crack comes from overhead/the bullet's flight line; the thump comes from the actual shooter direction — so they can even pan differently. Reproducing this gap turns 'enemy is shooting' into 'enemy is ~500m, up that ridgeline' — exactly the field-manual literacy the bar demands.
techniques.webAudioMapping: The repo ALREADY has Spatial.crackAt / Spatial.thumpAt / split in synth.ts — the mechanism exists. Extensions: (1) compute thumpAt = crackAt + dist/343 (player.ts), clamp to perceptible only when split=true; (2) pan the crack toward the round's flight bearing and the thump toward the shooter's map bearing (StereoPannerNode pan computed separately for the two layers); (3) make the muzzle_insurgent/muzzle_us report (BODY+SUB) play at thumpAt while the N-wave crack plays at crackAt, instead of both at crack. No new nodes — re-wire which layer uses which offset.
techniques.source: Crack & Thump (Max Velocity Tactical) https://maxvelocitytactical.com/crack-thump/ ; existing lib/audio/synth.ts Spatial interface

techniques.name: Procedural convolution-reverb tail (decaying-noise IR) for the 'rolling thunder' valley
techniques.howItWorks: A reverb tail is just a decaying-noise impulse response convolved with the dry sound — noise has 'no eigenfrequencies and infinitely high density,' so an exp-decaying noise buffer IS a near-perfect reverb tail. For a Korengal valley you want a LONG, bright-to-dull tail: the gunshot's energy bounces off ridgelines giving 0.5-3s of decay with discrete slap-echoes. This is what makes distant fire read as 'pop... then rolling thunder' rather than a dry click. A ConvolverNode with a procedurally generated IR delivers this with ZERO audio-file assets — fully within the no-samples constraint.
techniques.webAudioMapping: Build ONE ConvolverNode at init with a procedurally generated IR: a stereo AudioBuffer ~1.8-2.6s long filled with white noise * exp-decay envelope (e^(-t/tau), tau≈0.6s), then progressively lowpass the buffer over its length (highs die first = air absorption in the tail). For valley character, ADD 3-5 discrete slap taps into the IR at 0.15/0.4/0.8/1.4s (ridge reflections, Mountains create multi-second decays with 0.5-3s echo spacing). Route every gunshot's BODY layer through a wet send: dry->master AND dry->sendGain->convolver->master, with sendGain scaled UP with distance (far shots = more tail, less direct). This is the single biggest missing immersion piece — the system has NO reverb today.
techniques.source: Decaying-noise IR theory (Sweetwater/LiquidSonics convolution IR guides) https://www.sweetwater.com/insync/create-idealized-impulse-responses-convolution-reverbs/ ; canyon-echo timing (Pixflow gunfire guide) https://pixflow.net/blog/gun-gunfire-sound-effects/ ; MDN Web Audio ConvolverNode

techniques.name: Distance = transient-softening + lowpass + tail-ratio (the 'pop becomes thunder' curve)
techniques.howItWorks: Distance does three coupled things, not just lower the volume: (1) air absorption progressively lowpasses highs (the sharp 4kHz crack erodes first); (2) the attack transient SOFTENS — near shots have a sub-5ms snap, far shots have a rounded 'pop' with longer attack and lost crack; (3) the tail/reverb RATIO rises — distant fire is mostly its own reflections. So a near M4 = bright snap+body+almost-dry; a ridge-line M4 at 800m = dull lowpassed pop with a big reverb tail and no audible mechanical layer. Modeling all three (not just gain) is what sells distance.
techniques.webAudioMapping: Per-cue in player.ts, derive from distance d: cutoff = lerp(18000Hz @0m -> 700Hz @1km) on the air-absorption lowpass (Spatial.cutoff already exists); attack = lerp(0.0005 -> 0.02) passed into noiseBurst; DROP the mechanical+N-wave layers entirely past ~250m (a soldier can't hear an AK's bolt at 600m); reverb sendGain = lerp(0.05 -> 0.6). At max distance, skip BODY's high formant and play mostly SUB + tail. Curves should be smooth functions of d so the sim's continuous geometry maps continuously to timbre.
techniques.source: Pixflow distant-gunfire guide (progressive lowpass, longer attack, boosted reverb ratio) https://pixflow.net/blog/gun-gunfire-sound-effects/ ; Gunshot frequency analysis (low freq travels farther) https://thegunzone.com/what-is-the-frequency-of-a-gunshot/

techniques.name: Caliber timbre via formant frequency + decay length (AK woody vs M4 bright, principled)
techniques.howItWorks: The 7.62x39 (AK) vs 5.56 (M4) difference is real spectral physics: 7.62 is a larger, lower-pressure-curve round producing a deeper, 'woodier,' longer report with peak energy lower in the 1-4kHz band; 5.56 is higher-pressure and shorter-barreled-typical, giving a brighter, sharper, higher-pitched crack with energy biased toward 3-5kHz. The right knobs are: (a) body bandpass CENTER frequency, (b) report DECAY length (7.62 rings a touch longer), (c) sub fundamental, (d) N-wave period (above). The repo's muzzle_us vs muzzle_insurgent split is already on this axis — the upgrade is making the deltas physically motivated and adding a parametric weapon table.
techniques.webAudioMapping: Make a per-weapon param record { bodyCenterHz, bodyQ, reportDur, subF0, subF1, nwaveDur, nwaveHP }. M4: body 3500Hz, reportDur 0.05, sub 180->90, nwave 0.00035/5kHz. AK: body 2600Hz, reportDur 0.075, sub 140->68, nwave 0.0006/3.5kHz. SAW(5.56): like M4 but tighter+brighter; PKM(7.62R): like AK but heavier sub + slower bolt. Feed those into the 5-layer stack. This is exactly the parametric-by-caliber approach of the Springer physically-motivated model (params = barrel length, bullet type, muzzle velocity). The repo already encodes RPM (SAW ~850, PKM ~650) in the burst step — extend that table to timbre.
techniques.source: AK vs M4 spectral character (GunZone, DefenceTalk) https://thegunzone.com/what-is-the-frequency-of-a-gunshot/ ; Procedural Synthesis of Gunshot Sounds Based on Physically Motivated Models (Springer) https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-319-53088-8_4

techniques.name: Mechanical bolt/action layer + brass tinkle (the detail that says 'real gun')
techniques.howItWorks: Real automatic fire has an audible mechanical rhythm UNDER the report: the bolt-carrier slamming, and (for the firer/very near) brass casings ejecting and pinging on rock. AAA gunshot stacks carry a dedicated 'mechanical' layer (slide/hammer/ejection) precisely because it's the difference between a synth 'pew' and a machine. For an automatic burst this mechanical clack at the cyclic rate gives the gun its mechanical signature even when the report itself is generic.
techniques.webAudioMapping: MECHANICAL clack = noiseBurst(bandpass ~2.5-3.5kHz metallic, Q4-6, dur 0.006, peak ~0.12) scheduled ~10-20ms after each report in a burst (so it reads as the bolt cycling between rounds, not on top of the shot). BRASS (near only, d<30m): 2-3 tiny noiseBurst(bandpass 4-7kHz, Q8, dur 0.01, peak 0.06) at jittered offsets 80-220ms after the shot, using cue.v for deterministic placement. Keep peaks LOW — this is detail, not a layer that competes with the report. Gate it off past ~60m (you don't hear brass across the valley).
techniques.source: Kilborn 5-layer model (mechanical layer) https://blog.prosoundeffects.com/how-to-sound-design-first-person-shooter-gunshot-sound-effects-with-mark-kilborn ; Splice weapon-design guide https://splice.com/blog/design-weapon-sound-video-games/

techniques.name: Granular per-shot variation to defeat the machine-gun-repetition artifact (deterministically)
techniques.howItWorks: Identical retriggered shots fatigue the ear and scream 'fake.' The pro fix is per-shot variation of pitch, filter cutoff, amplitude, decay, and micro-timing — Leonard Paul's granulation insight is that random grain selection makes repeated sounds feel 'organic, like water over rocks,' avoiding 'unnatural repetitiveness.' For a synth (not sample) engine you get this for free by jittering synthesis params per shot. CRITICAL for this repo: the jitter MUST be deterministic (driven by cue.v / event index), never Math.random in the mapper — same seed must reproduce the firefight's exact sound.
techniques.webAudioMapping: The repo already has the right hook: cue.v is a deterministic 0..1 and the j(lo,hi) helper in synth.ts. Extend it so EACH shot in a burst gets its own deterministic offset: derive per-shot v_i = fract(cue.v*PHI + i*0.61803) (golden-ratio decorrelation, pure function of cue.v and shot index i). Use v_i to jitter: body center +/-8%, peak +/-15%, decay +/-12%, micro-timing +/-4ms, pan +/-0.05. The white-noise BUFFER may use Math.random (it's render-side per CLAUDE.md), but the PARAM choices must come from v_i so the audible result is seed-reproducible.
techniques.source: Granulation of Sound in Video Games — Leonard J. Paul, AES 41st (2011) https://videogameaudio.com/AES-Feb2011/AES41-04Feb11-GranulationOfSoundInVideoGames-LeonardJPaul.pdf ; KVR avoiding-machine-gun-effect thread

techniques.name: WaveShaper soft-clip on the body for 'felt-in-the-chest' weight (already used for IED, extend to MGs)
techniques.howItWorks: A muzzle report at real SPL is a clipped/saturated event — the harmonic distortion of soft-clipping adds upper harmonics that read as loudness and 'bite' even at safe playback levels, the perceptual trick that makes a -20dBFS sample feel like a 160dB gun. The repo already does this for the IED (tanh waveshaper). Applying a gentler soft-clip to the BODY layer of near gunfire (especially the SAW/PKM rips) adds the aggressive crunch that distinguishes a belt-fed weapon's authority from a single rifle.
techniques.webAudioMapping: Reuse the existing WaveShaperNode tanh-curve pattern from the 'ied' case in synth.ts, but milder: curve[i] = tanh(x * 1.4) for near body layers; tanh(x*2.2) stays for IED. Route only the BODY+SUB through the shaper (NOT the tail/reverb send — you want the dry shot to bite, the reflections to stay clean). Scale the drive amount UP with proximity and DOWN with distance (far shots aren't clipping at the listener). Follow with a shared DynamicsCompressorNode on the master gunfire bus to glue overlapping shots and prevent clipping when many fire at once.
techniques.source: Web Audio WaveShaperNode distortion (MDN/Noisehack) https://noisehack.com/generate-noise-web-audio-api/ ; existing 'ied' recipe in lib/audio/synth.ts; Splice weapon-design (saturation for weight)

techniques.name: Exponential-decay envelope discipline (percussive shape, ~20ms time constant)
techniques.howItWorks: Gunshots are percussive: the muzzle blast envelope is a near-instant attack then an EXPONENTIAL decay (real-world detection systems model the muzzle-blast decay with a ~20ms time constant; the body 'within milliseconds'). Linear ramps sound synthetic/buzzy; exponential decay is what gives a natural percussive 'thwack.' The shape per layer differs: transient ~3-5ms total, body ~20-50ms, sub ~50-80ms, tail seconds. Getting the decay SHAPE right matters more than the spectrum for 'realness.'
techniques.webAudioMapping: The repo's noiseBurst/tone already use g.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime — keep that, it's correct. Tune time constants per layer to the physics: transient dur 0.004, body dur 0.03-0.05 (M4) / 0.05-0.075 (AK), sub dur 0.06-0.08. For an even more natural curve consider gain.setTargetAtTime(0, at, tau) with tau≈0.02 (the documented muzzle-blast time constant) instead of a hard exponentialRampTo endpoint, since setTargetAtTime gives a true RC-decay. Avoid linearRampToValueAtTime for any gunshot amplitude.
techniques.source: Gunshot detection envelope (20ms decay time constant) https://thegunzone.com/what-is-the-frequency-of-a-gunshot/ ; MDN Advanced Techniques (exponential percussive decay) https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_Audio_API/Advanced_techniques

techniques.name: Farnell layered-blast architecture for HE (shockwave + blast + fireball + pressure-wave)
techniques.howItWorks: Andy Farnell's canonical explosion (Designing Sound) decomposes a blast into 4 timed layers that map directly onto the repo's blast_small/large/ied/RPG cues: (1) SHOCKWAVE — sharp 10ms attack transient (the crack); (2) BLAST — noise through a cutoff sweeping UP to ~7kHz, soft-clipped, with a long decay (up to seconds); (3) FIREBALL — noise bandpassed ~70Hz, triggered ~100ms LATE for warmth; (4) PRESSURE-WAVE — a feedback-delay low rumble (10Hz-10kHz band) sustaining seconds. The key insight is the staggered TIMING (shock immediate, fireball +100ms, rumble trailing) — that delay structure is what makes a blast feel huge rather than like a single noise pop.
techniques.webAudioMapping: Restructure blast_large/ied as 4 staggered layers: SHOCKWAVE = noiseBurst(highpass, dur 0.006, sharp). BLAST = a noise source whose filter freq exponentialRampToValueAtTime sweeps 200->7000Hz over ~0.2s through a tanh shaper. FIREBALL = noiseBurst(bandpass 70Hz, Q1, dur 0.4) scheduled at crack+0.1. PRESSURE-WAVE = sub() sine 55->22Hz long + a DelayNode feedback loop (gain 0.85, lowpass 10kHz) for the trailing rumble, or route through the valley convolver for the rolling echo. The repo's IED already approximates this but flat-in-time — adding the +100ms fireball and trailing rumble is the upgrade.
techniques.source: Andy Farnell, Designing Sound — Practical 31 Explosions https://aspress.co.uk/sd/practical31.html ; existing blast_* recipes in lib/audio/synth.ts

techniques.name: Automatic-fire as ramp-up / loop / ramp-down with first-shot emphasis
techniques.howItWorks: Game-audio convention for automatic weapons is a 3-stage model: a distinct FIRST shot (loudest, fullest, gets the transient+tail), a LOOP of cyclic shots (slightly reduced, varied), and a TAIL-OFF (last shot gets an extra-long tail as the gun stops). The first-shot emphasis matters because the opening round of a burst is the one the brain locks onto; making every shot identical loses that. The repo already bursts N shots with falling gain — adding genuine first-shot fullness + a final long tail completes the arc.
techniques.webAudioMapping: In the mg_us/mg_insurgent loops: give shot i=0 the full 5-layer stack INCLUDING a tail send; shots 1..n-2 a lighter stack (drop mechanical-detail/brass, reduce tail send, apply the v_i jitter); the LAST shot n-1 gets a long reverb send (big tail as fire ceases). Keep the existing deterministic step (RPM) and falling-gain envelope. This is pure scheduling logic over the primitives already present — no new node types.
techniques.source: Macprovideo/game-audio automatic-fire 3-stage (ramp-up/loop/ramp-down) https://macprovideo.com/article/game-audio/game-audio-creating-a-realistic-rate-of-fire-for-automatic-weapons-using-logic ; existing mg_* recipes

keyInsights: The repo already has the RIGHT bones for a 20x leap: shared noise buffer, exponential-decay noiseBurst/tone/sub primitives, deterministic cue.v jitter, and a Spatial interface with crackAt/thumpAt/split/cutoff. The work is RESTRUCTURING flat single-burst recipes into proper layered stacks and ADDING a reverb tail — not a ground-up rewrite. (lib/audio/synth.ts)

The single biggest missing immersion piece is REVERB: there is no tail today. A ConvolverNode with a procedurally-generated decaying-noise IR (1.8-2.6s, exp decay, progressive lowpass, plus 3-5 discrete ridge-slap taps at 0.15/0.4/0.8/1.4s) delivers the 'pop... then rolling thunder' of a Korengal valley with ZERO audio-file assets — fully inside the no-samples constraint.

A gunshot is FIVE time-aligned layers (transient / body / sub / mechanical / tail), and a passing round is a SEPARATE physical event (the supersonic N-wave: a sub-millisecond ~0.3-0.5ms snap) distinct from the muzzle report. Treating crack and report as the same sound is the core current limitation; splitting them by speed-of-sound (crackAt vs thumpAt, both already in the Spatial interface) is the highest-realism, lowest-cost win.

Distance is THREE coupled transforms, not just gain: progressive lowpass (air absorption, highs die first), transient softening (sharp snap -> rounded pop, drop N-wave/mechanical/brass past ~250m), and rising tail-to-direct ratio. Mapping the sim's continuous geometry to these continuous timbre curves is what makes a ridgeline AK at 800m read as distance, not just quietness — and crack-thump gap (~0.5s@300m, ~1s@600m) becomes a real in-fiction ranging cue a soldier would recognize.

AK-vs-M4 (and SAW-vs-PKM) timbre is physically principled, not vibes: 7.62 = lower body-formant (~2.6kHz), longer report decay, deeper sub, longer N-wave period (woodier); 5.56 = higher formant (~3.5kHz), shorter sharper report, shorter N-wave (brighter). Drive it from a per-weapon param table {bodyCenterHz, reportDur, subF0/F1, nwaveDur, nwaveHP}, extending the RPM table the repo already has.

All per-shot variation MUST be deterministic (golden-ratio decorrelation of cue.v + shot-index), never Math.random in the mapper — the white-noise buffer may use Math.random because it's render-side, but param CHOICES feeding audible timbre must be a pure function so a seed reproduces the firefight's exact sound (determinism contract).
pitfalls: DETERMINISM BREAK: putting Math.random() in param selection (pitch/filter/timing jitter) instead of deriving from cue.v + shot index. CLAUDE.md is explicit — only the render-side noise BUFFER may use Math.random; the event->cue mapping and all audible param choices must be pure. A same-seed firefight that sounds different IS the bug.

ARCADE-Y FEEL: over-bright, over-compressed, sample-game 'pew-pew.' This game's soul is 'the readable silence of the calm-before' and Restrepo/The Outpost restraint. Keep peaks low, let the TAIL and the crack-thump GAP carry weight, never let every shot be a max-loudness transient. Restraint is a literal success criterion here.

PERF: one ConvolverNode reused for ALL gunfire via wet sends is fine; spinning up a NEW ConvolverNode per shot (or rebuilding the IR per shot) will tank a busy firefight. Build the IR ONCE at init. Likewise share the single white-noise AudioBuffer (already done) and put a single DynamicsCompressorNode on the gunfire master bus to handle polyphony glue rather than clipping.

POLYPHONY/CLIPPING: a heavy TIC can schedule dozens of overlapping 5-layer voices; without a master limiter/compressor on the gunfire bus the sum clips into digital crackle (which ironically sounds arcade-y). Cap simultaneous voices and/or thin distant shots to fewer layers.

MIX MUD: stacking sub layers from many simultaneous shots piles up 40-120Hz energy into boom. High-pass the reverb send, drop the SUB layer on distant shots, and don't give every shot in a burst a full sub — reserve fullness for first-shot emphasis.

OVER-MODELING THE N-WAVE: the supersonic crack is real but ~0.3-0.5ms — do NOT try to model the full Whitham N-wave waveform sample-by-sample; a single ultra-short high-passed noise burst with caliber-tuned duration captures the perceptual snap. Conversely, don't fire the crack layer for shots NOT passing near the listener (only near-miss/incoming geometry).

STALE BASELINE: per CLAUDE.md Law 1/5, capture a before recording (a headless render of representative cues to a buffer, or a live capture via scripts/shoot.mjs) BEFORE editing synth.ts, so the 20x claim is provable as a delta and not vibes. There is no numeric audio harness today — building one (render cues offline, dump spectral/RMS/peak) is core work, not a detour.

techniques.name: Shared convolution-reverb send bus with a procedurally-generated decaying-noise IR (the canyon tail)
techniques.howItWorks: Build ONE ConvolverNode whose IR is exponentially-decaying filtered noise: for each sample j, ir[j] = (noise in [-1,1]) * decayBase^j, where decayBase = (1/1000)^(1/(RT60*sampleRate)) so amplitude hits -60 dB exactly at RT60 (Moorer's result: exp-decaying white noise is a surprisingly good reverb tail). Add a short linear fade-in (5-15 ms) to soften the onset, and a gradual lowpass swept from ~bright to ~dull across the tail so highs die faster than lows (air + wall absorption). Every cue's gain node taps a parallel send into this single shared bus; the dry path is unchanged. This is the cheapest 20x: one convolver processes the whole 30-man firefight, not per voice.
techniques.webAudioMapping: Generate IR once at unlock via OfflineAudioContext or a plain AudioBuffer fill: `const N=Math.round(RT60*sr*1.5); buf=ctx.createBuffer(2,N,sr); for(ch){d=buf.getChannelData(ch); base=Math.pow(1/1000,1/(RT60*sr)); for(j) d[j]=(Math.random()*2-1)*Math.pow(base,j);}` then optionally re-render through an OfflineAudioContext BiquadFilter(lowpass) whose .frequency ramps lpStart->lpEnd. Node graph: build a persistent `reverbBus = ctx.createGain()` -> `convolver(buf)` -> `wetGain` -> master. In schedule(), after the existing `cueGain -> lp -> pan -> master`, add one branch `cueGain.connect(reverbSend); reverbSend.connect(reverbBus)` where reverbSend.gain encodes the per-cue wet amount. RT60 ~1.6-2.2 s for a tight Korengal draw, lpStart~6kHz, lpEnd~700Hz. Cost: one convolver + one gain per voice (the send), vs one whole convolver per voice.
techniques.source: reverbGen (adelespinasse) src/lib/index.ts generateReverb() — decayBase=(1/1000)^(1/decaySampleFrames), Moorer 'About This Reverberation Business'; gskinner 'Making Reverb with the Web Audio API'; MDN ConvolverNode

techniques.name: Distance-driven wet/dry (direct-to-reverberant ratio) + pre-delay as the primary distance cue
techniques.howItWorks: The dominant perceptual cue for source distance is the direct-to-reverberant ratio (DRR): close sources are mostly dry, far sources are heard mostly through their reflections. So instead of (or alongside) the current pure attenuation, scale the reverb-send level UP with distance while the dry level falls — at the edge of audibility a shot is almost all tail. Pre-delay (gap between dry hit and first reflection) should also grow with distance: a far source's reflections arrive relatively sooner after its already-delayed dry sound, but the canyon-wall bounce adds a real geometric pre-delay. This single ratio change does more for 'it's across the valley' than any EQ trick.
techniques.webAudioMapping: Compute in the existing spatial() using `norm = distM/AUDIBLE_M` already there. dryGain = atten (current behavior). wetSend = clamp(0.15 + 0.85*norm, 0, 1) * cue.gain — near 0.15, far ~1.0. Insert a per-cue (or per-distance-bucket) `DelayNode` of preDelay = clamp(0.02 + norm*0.12, 0.02, 0.18) s on the send path: `cueGain -> sendGain -> preDelay -> reverbBus`. Optionally also lowpass the SEND (not just the dry) harder with distance since the tail of a distant event is duller. This reuses the camera-as-listener distance already computed; no sim change, deterministic mapper untouched.
techniques.source: Audiokinetic 'A Wwise Approach to Spatial Audio Part 1 — Distance Modeling'; arXiv P-Reverb (Perceptual characterization of early/late reflections); zleague Gray Zone Warfare gunfire-reverb postmortem

techniques.name: Discrete canyon slap-back taps (multi-tap DelayNode) for rolling mountain echoes — the Restrepo signature
techniques.howItWorks: Real valley firefights are NOT a smooth tail — you hear discrete cracks rolling away as the report bounces off named cliff faces. Physics: a wall at distance D returns a slap at t = 2D/343 s (a wall 170 m off = 1.0 s; 340 m = 2.0 s). Two perceptibly-separate echoes need >~0.1 s (~17 m) of path difference. Model 2-4 discrete taps at canyon-scale delays with decreasing gain and increasing lowpass (each bounce loses highs), placed at slightly different pans (the echo comes from a different wall than the source). This is what makes it read as MOUNTAINS, not a room. Feed these taps INTO the convolution bus to also seed the diffuse tail (early reflections increase the late echo density) — discrete slaps up front, smooth tail behind.
techniques.webAudioMapping: A parallel 'canyon' send: `cueGain -> canyonSend -> [tap1, tap2, tap3]`. Each tap = `DelayNode(delayTime=Ti) -> BiquadFilter(lowpass, freq=Fi) -> StereoPanner(panOffset_i) -> tapGain_i -> master AND -> reverbBus`. Use deterministic geometric-ish taps, e.g. T=[0.18, 0.42, 0.85] s (scaled to a per-valley 'wall distance' parameter), tapGain=[0.5,0.3,0.16], lowpass F=[4000,2200,1200] Hz. For louder events (ied/blast_large/mg) raise tap gains and add a 4th long tap (~1.4 s) for the 'thunder rolling out' beat; for tiny events (impact/ricochet) skip taps entirely. ONE shared multi-tap rig can serve all voices (taps are linear) — only the per-cue canyonSend.gain varies. Pure: tap delays/gains are constants or a pure function of cue.kind, no PRNG.
techniques.source: CK-12 / canyon echo physics (t=2D/c, 17 m min separation); Valhalla DSP 'Schroeder Reverbs: the forgotten algorithm' (slap/echo density); Gearspace 'simulating outdoor spaces' (multi-tap exterior slaps); Restrepo soldier accounts (gunfire echoing from below the post)

techniques.name: Per-event reverb CHARACTER, not just one global verb (event-keyed RT60 / wet amount)
techniques.howItWorks: Different events excite the valley differently and need different verbs: a rifle crack throws a short bright tail; a 120mm/IED blast throws a long, low, slow rolling tail that physically dominates the valley for seconds; a near MG burst smears into a continuous wash. Rather than one IR, key the wet-send amount and (optionally) tail length to cue.kind: small arms get modest wet + short taps; HE gets heavy wet + the long 4th tap; radio/dangerclose/tic_sting get ZERO reverb (they're 'in your headset', non-positional — keep them dry and present). This preserves the restrained mix: only the world-positional weapons bloom into the canyon.
techniques.webAudioMapping: Add a `KIND_WET: Record<CueKind,number>` table beside the existing KIND_TRIM in player.ts: e.g. muzzle_*: 0.35, mg_*: 0.45, blast_small: 0.6, blast_large/ied: 0.85, impact/ricochet: 0.15, splash: 0.7, smoke_pop/flare: 0.1, radio/dangerclose/tic_sting/shot: 0.0. The send gain = wetSend(distance) * KIND_WET[kind]. Optionally maintain TWO shared convolver buses (a 'short' RT60~1.2 s and a 'long' RT60~2.8 s) and route HE to the long one, small arms to the short — still only 2 convolvers total. Mirrors the existing KIND_TRIM pattern exactly; an exhaustive Record makes the compiler force every new CueKind to declare its wetness.
techniques.source: pixflow gun-sound guide (environment-dependent gunfire resonance); Audiokinetic Wwise reverb zones; existing player.ts KIND_TRIM pattern (lib/audio/player.ts:22)

techniques.name: Algorithmic Schroeder/Freeverb tail (comb+allpass) as a CONVOLVER-FREE fallback / modulated alternative
techniques.howItWorks: If you want a hand-tunable, zero-buffer tail (no IR pre-render, parameters changeable live), build a Freeverb-style reverb from native nodes: 8 parallel lowpass-feedback comb filters summed, then 4 allpass filters in series. Freeverb's tuned comb delays (samples @44.1k) are {1116,1188,1277,1356,1422,1491,1557,1617} and allpass delays {556,441,341,225}; right channel adds a stereospread of 23 samples. The comb feedback g sets RT60 via g = 10^(-3*delaySec/RT60); the in-comb lowpass 'damping' makes highs decay faster (the mountain air-absorption). Modulating the comb delay times slowly (a tiny LFO) removes the metallic ring and is a known trick for natural tails. FDN (4-8 mutually-prime delay lines + a Householder/Hadamard feedback matrix, g_i = 10^(-3*Mi/(fs*RT60))) is the higher-quality cousin if the combs ring.
techniques.webAudioMapping: Comb = `input -> DelayNode(d) -> BiquadFilter(lowpass=damp) -> fbGain(g) -> back to the DelayNode input (createGain loop)`, output tapped after the delay. Build 8 in parallel into a summing gain, then chain 4 allpass = `DelayNode + feedforward/feedback gains (0.5)` in series. Web Audio has no native allpass-delay, so realize each as the 2-gain lattice around a DelayNode. Convert Freeverb sample delays to seconds: 1116/44100=0.0253 s, etc. Slowly modulate each comb delayTime with an OscillatorNode->gain->delay.delayTime (depth ~0.3 ms, rate ~0.1-0.5 Hz). Heavier CPU than a convolver (≈20+ nodes in feedback) but fully live-tweakable and needs no pre-render; keep it as ONE shared bus, never per-voice.
techniques.source: Freeverb tuning (thestk/stk FreeVerb.cpp; ccrma.stanford.edu/~jos/pasp/Freeverb.html); Valhalla DSP Schroeder article; dsprelated.com FDN Reverberation (g_i=10^(-3 Mi T/t60), Householder/Hadamard, mutually-prime delays)

techniques.name: Elevation / high-ground cue via the terrain elevation field (the gun from the ridge)
techniques.howItWorks: Today there is NO elevation cue, yet in the Korengal the defining tactical fact is who holds the high ground — the PKM 'from above' should sound different. A source far above the valley floor has a longer, less-obstructed reflection path and reaches the listener with more open-air slap and less ground-coupled low-end; a source down in a draw is muffled and gets a tighter, darker tail. Use the render-accessible terrain elevation (Terrain.elev / minElev / floor elevations) to derive a relative-height term and bend the wet amount, tap delays, and dry lowpass with it — purely render-side, sim untouched.
techniques.webAudioMapping: In player.spatial(), sample `dz = terrain.elev[idx(cue.pos)] - terrain.elev[idx(camCenter)]` (terrain is already on the render side via the World). For sources above the listener (dz>0): raise wetSend slightly and brighten the first canyon tap (open-air path) — `tap1 lowpass += dz*scale`, and shorten its pre-delay a touch. For sources below (dz<0, down in a draw): darken the dry lowpass (extra -Hz) and reduce high-frequency tap content (terrain occlusion proxy). Keep it a gentle continuous mapping, not a switch. This is an additive multiplier on the same send/tap nodes from the techniques above — no new bus.
techniques.source: Terrain elevation API in repo (lib/sim/terrain.ts: elev Float32Array, minElev, floorSouth/floorNorth); Restrepo/The Outpost high-ground tactical accounts; general acoustic elevation/occlusion modeling (Wwise spatial audio)

techniques.name: Bake early reflections into the IR (discrete pre-tail taps inside the convolver buffer)
techniques.howItWorks: Instead of a separate multi-tap rig, you can encode the discrete canyon slaps DIRECTLY into the procedurally-generated IR by writing impulse spikes at the slap-back sample offsets before the diffuse decaying-noise tail. The IR then becomes: a few sparse, decreasing-amplitude impulses (the named cliff walls) followed by the exp-decay noise floor (the diffuse valley wash). One convolver then produces both the rolling discrete echoes AND the smooth tail in a single pass — the most efficient possible realization. Trade-off: the slap delays are then fixed per-IR (can't follow per-source wall geometry), so it's best when the valley has a characteristic acoustic you set per-deployment.
techniques.webAudioMapping: When filling the IR buffer: first write the noise*decay tail as in technique 1, then ADD spikes: `for each wall {k=Math.round(Tk*sr); ir[k]+=ampK; ir[k+1]+=ampK*0.5;}` with Tk=[0.18,0.42,0.85] s and ampK=[0.6,0.35,0.2], optionally panned by writing different amplitudes into L vs R channels. Result: one `convolver(buf)` shared bus does discrete + diffuse. Regenerate a small set of IRs (e.g. 'tight draw', 'open valley', 'wadi') at unlock and switch the convolver.buffer per deployment/zone. Determinism preserved: IR generation is render-side noise (allowed), the choice of IR is a pure function of the deployment seed/zone.
techniques.source: Audiokinetic Wwise (early reflections fed into late reverb to increase echo density); Moorer early-reflection + diffuse-tail model; reverbGen IR fill loop

keyInsights: Use a SHARED reverb send bus, never per-voice convolution. Wwise explicitly applies reflection/reverb per-emitter on an Auxiliary Bus because per-voice 'would be too heavy' — for a 30-man firefight one ConvolverNode (or one Freeverb rig) processes every source via a cheap per-cue send gain. This is the single most important architectural decision and it fits the existing per-cue `cueGain -> lp -> pan -> master` chain by adding one parallel `cueGain -> sendGain -> reverbBus` branch.

The procedural IR is a one-liner of math, not a mystery: ir[j] = noise * ((1/1000)^(1/(RT60*sr)))^j gives an exact -60 dB-at-RT60 exp-decay tail (Moorer). Add a short fade-in and a tail-swept lowpass. No audio file needed — fully satisfies the no-binary-assets constraint, and the noise is render-side only so determinism (Law 7) holds.

Distance is carried by the wet/dry ratio (DRR), not just attenuation. Today the sim only attenuates + lowpasses with distance; bloom the reverb SEND up as the source recedes (near ~0.15 wet, far ~1.0 wet) and grow pre-delay — that's what makes a shot read as 'across the valley' rather than just 'quiet'. The distance term is already computed in player.spatial().

Canyon character = DISCRETE rolling slap-backs in front of a diffuse tail, not a single smooth verb. Physics gives the timing for free: a cliff wall at distance D slaps at t=2D/343 s, so Korengal-scale walls (170-340 m) produce 1-2 s echoes that must be perceptibly separate (>0.1 s apart). Model 2-4 multi-tap DelayNodes (decreasing gain, increasing lowpass, slightly different pans) and let them also seed the convolver tail.

Key the wet amount to cue.kind via an exhaustive Record (mirroring the existing KIND_TRIM): small arms get modest short tails, HE/IED get heavy long rolling tails, and radio/dangerclose/tic_sting get ZERO reverb (they're 'in your headset'). This keeps the restrained 'readable silence' mix — only world-positional weapons bloom into the valley.

Two free, on-theme upgrades the current system entirely lacks: an ELEVATION cue (the terrain elev field is render-accessible — the gun from the high ground sounds more open, the draw sounds muffled) and per-deployment valley acoustics (regenerate 'tight draw' vs 'open valley' IRs at unlock). Both are render-side only and need no sim/determinism changes.
pitfalls: Per-voice ConvolverNodes will tank performance — a convolver is expensive and instantiating one per cue in a 30-man TIC (MAX_VOICES=24) is the classic mistake. Always tap a SHARED reverb bus; the per-cue cost is one GainNode send.

Generating the IR (filling a multi-second noise buffer or running an OfflineAudioContext) is NOT free — do it ONCE at unlock(), cache it like the existing shared `_noise` buffer in synth.ts. Never regenerate per cue or per frame.

Determinism break risk: the IR uses Math.random() — that is fine ONLY on the render side (synth/player already do this for noiseBuffer). Never let reverb parameters or IR choice flow back into lib/sim or the pure mapper. The cue->sound mapping must stay a pure function (Law 7); reverb lives entirely after the cue is emitted.

Over-wet = arcade mush, the exact opposite of the brief. The references warn quiet/close sounds should get little-to-no reverb; drowning every rifle crack in tail kills the 'readable silence of the calm-before'. Default wet low and let only distance + HE push it up; keep radio/UI cues bone dry.

Metallic ringing from comb/allpass (algorithmic) tails — if you go the Freeverb/FDN route, use mutually-prime delay lengths and slowly modulate the comb delay times, or the tail sounds like a flanger/tin can, which reads as cheap/arcade-y. The convolution IR avoids this entirely.

Clipping/buildup in a sustained firefight: many simultaneous wet sends summing into one bus can pile up and clip the master. Put a DynamicsCompressorNode (gentle, fast) on the reverb bus output, and scale the bus gain down as activeVoices rises (mirror the existing polyphony-cap LOD philosophy).

Don't let the tail bleed through the pause/warp gate. The existing tick() gate stops scheduling on pause/warp; long reverb tails already in flight will ring out — either keep them (natural) or mute the reverb bus on pause. Pick deliberately so a paused screenshot isn't accidentally noisy.

Pre-delay + speed-of-sound double-count: the system already delays the 'thump' by distM/343 (crack-thump split). If you ALSO add a big reverb pre-delay scaled by distance you can smear the timing unnaturally. Keep reverb pre-delay modest (~20-180 ms) and let the existing thump delay own the gross speed-of-sound offset.

techniques.name: Three-tier ambient architecture: persistent BED loops + Poisson-scheduled SPOT one-shots + sim-driven DYNAMIC params
techniques.howItWorks: The canonical game-ambience model splits a soundscape into three roles: (1) a continuous BED of stereo loops (wind, river, generator, room tone) that is always present; (2) discrete SPOT one-shots (a single bird call, a dog bark, a creak, a far gust) edited OUT of the bed and re-injected with randomized timing so no recognizable pattern survives; (3) DYNAMIC parameters (time-of-day, weather, wind speed) that continuously re-mix the bed and re-weight the one-shot pools. Detailed/identifiable events live in the spot layer precisely because a recognizable sound baked into a loop is what the ear catches as repetition. This is the architecture STALKER, Firewatch and RDR all use.
techniques.webAudioMapping: Mirror the existing PURE/RENDER split. NEW pure module lib/audio/ambient-state.ts (sibling of mapper.ts) is a function of (secondsOfDay, solarLight, weather.label, weather.wind, isNight, camera-vs-COP/village/river distances) → an AmbientMix target: {windGain, riverGain, rainGain, generatorGain, biophonyDensity, anthrophonyEnable, reverbWet}. It emits ONLY deterministic numbers — no noise, no wall-clock. NEW render module lib/audio/ambient.ts owns a persistent voice bank wired ONCE at unlock: each BED voice = noiseBuffer→Biquad chain→GainNode→master (long-lived, never torn down, gains ramped via setTargetAtTime). SPOT one-shots reuse the existing synthCue/one-shot path but are TRIGGERED render-side by a Poisson timer (see technique 6). The existing AudioEngine.tick() gains an ambient.update(mix) call after the cue loop; the bed lives parallel to the 24-voice combat pool so it is never starved by the MAX_VOICES cap.
techniques.source: Game Audio Learning Portal — How To Make Ambiences For Games; STALKER Anomaly Immersive Ambience design (ModDB); RDR audio director interview (designingsound.org)

techniques.name: Procedural valley WIND: parallel bandpass-filter bank on noise, intensity ~1/f, with a lag between gust-envelope and filter-center movement
techniques.howItWorks: Farnell's canonical wind model (ported widely to Pd/Max/Csound): run continuous noise through a BANK of 10-50 parallel 2nd-order bandpass filters. A slow 1/f-ish (pink) random 'intensity' signal drives overall amplitude (the gusts); the bandpass CENTER frequencies and the high 'whistle' resonators are modulated more sharply but with a deliberate DELAY behind the intensity envelope — the perceptual cue that a gust builds, THEN the pitch rises as it whistles past objects. Low filters (~100-400 Hz) give the valley howl; a couple of high resonant peaks (~1-3 kHz, high Q) give the whistle around the wire/rocks. Crucially: drive overall wind gain AND brightness from the sim's actual wind speed so a Clear-3 m/s day and a Snow-7 m/s night are audibly different and LEARNABLE (the sim already models diurnal anabatic/katabatic flow).
techniques.webAudioMapping: ONE shared looping AudioBufferSourceNode of brown/pink noise (generate once, like the existing _noise buffer but -6dB/oct shaped). Fan it into 3-5 parallel BiquadFilters (cheap approximation of the 10-50 bank): 2x lowpass/bandpass @ 180 Hz & 350 Hz (Q~0.7) for the howl, 2x bandpass @ 900 Hz & 2200 Hz (Q~6-10) for the whistle. Each filter → its own GainNode → summed into windGain → master. GUSTS: a second slow noise buffer (or 2-3 detuned LFO OscillatorNodes @ 0.05-0.3 Hz summed) drives windGain via a GainNode on its .gain; map sim weather.wind (0-8 m/s) to base windGain AND nudge the whistle filter cutoffs up with speed. LAG: feed the gust signal to the whistle-filter .frequency through a DelayNode (~0.3-0.8 s) so brightness trails loudness. All param moves use setTargetAtTime so wind speed/weather changes glide. windVector() x-component can bias StereoPanner for directional gusts.
techniques.source: Andy Farnell, Designing Sound (MIT Press, wind chapter); Cycling74 'Synthetic Wind' forum (florian1947 summary: 10-50 parallel 2nd-order bandpass, intensity~1/f, delays between intensity & filter movement)

techniques.name: Acoustic-niche frequency partitioning: give every layer its own band so the bed never muds
techniques.howItWorks: Krause's acoustic niche hypothesis: in a healthy natural soundscape, species/sources partition the spectrum so they don't mask each other. Use it as a MIX DISCIPLINE, not biology: assign each ambient layer a reserved frequency band and bandpass-limit it there. Generator owns the low hum (~50-250 Hz + harmonics), river owns the broadband mid-high hiss (~400 Hz-6 kHz) but is gently notched where birds sing, wind howl owns ~100-400 Hz and whistle owns ~1-3 kHz, insects own a narrow ~4-7 kHz shimmer, birds own ~2-5 kHz transients, the adhan/dogs own the vocal mid (~300 Hz-2 kHz). When two layers must coexist (river + birds), notch the bed so the foreground reads. This is exactly the project's stated 'avoid mix mud' pitfall solved by design rather than by EQ-fighting at runtime, and it keeps the bed legible under the combat layer (the calm-before must stay readable).
techniques.webAudioMapping: Each persistent BED voice terminates in a band-limiting Biquad before its layer GainNode: generator→lowpass 250 Hz; river→bandpass center ~1.2 kHz wide Q~0.4 PLUS a peaking-filter NOTCH at 3-4 kHz (negative gain) to clear room for birds; wind already split as above. A single shared 'foreground duck': when a high-priority spot (adhan, near dog, or a combat cue) fires, ramp the river/wind GainNodes down ~3-5 dB via setTargetAtTime(target, now, 0.15) and back — reuse the radio-duck pattern already implied by KIND_TRIM. No global compressor needed for separation; the bands do the work.
techniques.source: Bernie Krause, Acoustic Niche Hypothesis (1993); Pijanowski et al., 'Soundscape Ecology', BioScience 2011 (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soundscape_ecology)

techniques.name: Non-repetition via UNSYNCHRONIZED loops + irrational loop lengths (no two layers share a period)
techniques.howItWorks: The core anti-loop-fatigue trick from natural-soundscape design: never let two looping beds share a period or phase. If wind loops every 11.3 s, river every 7.9 s, insects every 13.1 s, and generator every 5.7 s, their combined pattern only truly repeats at the least-common-multiple — effectively never within a session. The ear locks onto coincidences (two loops restarting together), so the fix is deliberately mutually-prime/irrational loop lengths and independent start phases. Combined with continuous LFO modulation on filter cutoffs, the bed 'evolves organically' and never reveals its seams. This is cheaper and more deterministic-friendly than granular and avoids shipping any sample.
techniques.webAudioMapping: Since every bed source is procedural looping noise, 'loop length' is really the period of the modulators on top of it. Give each layer's gust/shimmer LFO an irrational rate (wind 0.13 Hz, river-swell 0.077 Hz, insect-shimmer 0.19 Hz, generator-wobble 0.043 Hz) and start each at ctx.currentTime + a fixed per-layer phase offset. For the noise buffers themselves, use DIFFERENT buffer lengths per layer (e.g. 2.0 s, 3.1 s, 5.3 s) and loopStart/loopEnd so the underlying texture also de-phases. Determinism note: these rates/phases are CONSTANTS in the render layer (not PRNG), so two same-seed sessions still sound identical — the 'randomness' is the irrational beat pattern, not entropy.
techniques.source: Game Audio Learning Portal (unsynchronized loops never repeat); Splice 'Procedural audio in games' (constant loudness fatigues; introduce quiet)

techniques.name: Time-of-day & weather CROSSFADE via equal-power gain ramps on a fixed voice bank (no source restart)
techniques.howItWorks: Rather than swapping in new loops at dawn/dusk/weather change (which clicks and needs reload), keep ALL bed voices permanently alive and crossfade their GAINS along an equal-power curve driven by the sim's continuous solarLight (0..1) and weather label. Day biophony (birds, insects) fades up as solarLight rises; night biophony (crickets, the lone dog) fades up as it falls; the river/generator stay roughly constant; rain fades in with weather.precip and pushes a broadband hiss bed up while ducking birds to near-silence. Equal-power (cos/sin) rather than linear crossfade prevents the perceived volume dip when two beds are both at 50%. Because solarLight is already a smooth smoothstep ramp (5-7am, 17-19.5pm), the audio transition is automatically gradual and matches the on-screen night-light render.
techniques.webAudioMapping: ambient-state.ts emits per-layer target gains as a PURE function of solarLight & weather. ambient.update() applies them with master.gain.setTargetAtTime(target, now, 8.0) — an ~8 s time-constant so weather/dawn glides over tens of seconds, not abruptly. For the day↔night biophony pair use equal-power: dayGain = sin(solarLight*PI/2)*amp, nightGain = cos(solarLight*PI/2)*amp, both applied as targets. Rain bed = filtered-noise voice whose gain target is weather.precip?fullRain:0, with a parallel ramp on birdDensity→0. NO source.start/stop on transitions — only AudioParam ramps, so zero clicks and zero reallocation. Weather.label switch in the pure layer picks the band/gain set; the render side just chases the targets.
techniques.source: Boris Smus, Web Audio API book ch.3 (equal-power crossfade cos/sin); MDN setTargetAtTime (time-constant); RDR ambience respects weather & time of day (designingsound.org)

techniques.name: Biophony as a Poisson SPOT scheduler with a deterministic, seed-stable arrival sequence
techniques.howItWorks: Birds/insects/dogs/distant-voices must NOT be in the loop — they're sparse one-shots whose magic is irregular timing. Model each pool as a Poisson process: an exponentially-distributed inter-arrival time scaled by a density that the dynamic layer sets (high bird density at dawn, near-zero at night/in rain; high insect density on warm clear days; rare lone dog at night). Each fired one-shot is itself synthesized (a short pitched chirp = a couple of fast frequency-swept sines through a bandpass; a dog bark = a noise+formant burst; a far human voice = filtered formant babble) and SPATIALIZED at a village/COP position so it pans and attenuates correctly. The determinism contract is honored by deriving the arrival schedule and each one-shot's pitch/pan from a PURE hash of (layerId, secondsOfDay-bucket, index) — the same trick cue.ts already uses (cueVar = hash of source id). Same seed + same clock ⇒ same birds.
techniques.webAudioMapping: ambient-state.ts owns a per-pool 'next-fire clock': nextFire = lastFire + (-ln(hashToUnit(layer,n)) / density) where hashToUnit reuses RNG.hashString (already re-exported through the world barrel for the mapper). When world clock passes nextFire it appends a spot AudioCue {kind:'bird'|'insect'|'dog'|'voice', pos: villageOrRidgePos, v: hash} to the cue stream — flowing through the EXISTING mapper→synth→spatial pipeline (StereoPanner + distance atten + air-absorption lowpass already built). New synthCue recipes: bird = 2-4 quick sine sweeps (e.g. 3.5k→2.8k over 60-120ms) through a bandpass Q~8; cricket = amplitude-gated 4.5 kHz sine pulse train; dog = lowpass noise burst + 300/600 Hz formant tones; distant voice/adhan-snippet = sawtooth through 2-3 peaking formant filters, heavily lowpassed for distance. Density comes from the pure layer; nothing here uses wall-clock or Math.random.
techniques.source: Game Audio Learning Portal (detailed sounds edited out of loops → randomized spot effects); existing lib/audio/cue.ts cueVar determinism pattern (docs/progress/2026-06-06-procedural-audio)

techniques.name: Procedural valley REVERB from a decaying-noise impulse response (place acoustics without a sample)
techniques.howItWorks: A ConvolverNode's IR can be PROCEDURALLY generated as exponentially-decaying filtered noise — no audio file shipped. This gives the whole soundscape a sense of PLACE: a wide steep-walled valley has a long, dark, slappy tail; a close ravine is short and bright. Convolving the ambient bed (and a wet send of distant gunfire/explosions) through a ~1.5-2.5 s exp-decay IR adds the canyon reverb that the project explicitly lacks today and that every reference game (the crack of a rifle ROLLING down the valley in Restrepo/The Outpost) relies on for authenticity. The IR can be re-shaped by weather (fog/snow = shorter, more absorbed tail; clear = longer) by regenerating it on weather change (offline render, cheap, infrequent).
techniques.webAudioMapping: Generate IR via OfflineAudioContext(2, sampleRate*reverbTime, sampleRate): fill a stereo buffer with white noise, multiply each sample by an exponential decay (sample[i] *= (1 - i/len)^p, p≈2-4 for a natural exp tail), then band-shape it (highpass ~400 Hz so the tail isn't boomy, lowpass ~5-6 kHz for air absorption / valley darkness) — exactly the gskinner recipe. Wire as a PARALLEL WET SEND, not inline: master split into (a) dry→destination and (b) a reverbSend GainNode→ConvolverNode→destination. Ambient bed and DISTANT combat cues feed a higher wet ratio (the rolling-thunder report); close cues stay mostly dry. reverbWet target comes from the pure layer (distance/weather). Regenerate the IR only on weather.label change. CPU is trivial — one convolver, one IR.
techniques.source: gskinner blog 'Making Reverb with the Web Audio API' (decaying-noise IR + HP500/LP5000 shaping, parallel wet send); adelespinasse/reverbGen; MDN ConvolverNode

techniques.name: Procedural RAIN/RIVER: filtered broadband 'bed' + Poisson droplet/burble grains layered
techniques.howItWorks: Both water sources use the same two-part recipe: a continuous filtered-noise BED for the mass (the steady river hiss / the rain wash) PLUS sparse synthesized GRAINS for the detail (individual close raindrops, river burbles over rocks). The bed alone sounds like static; the grains alone sound sparse; together they read as water. Audiokinetic's pure-synthesis rain uses exactly this: a noise bed for the downpour plus short pitched-noise droplets triggered with randomized density and pitch. For the river, modulate the bed's bandpass center slowly (the water 'breathing') and add low burble grains; tie river GAIN/brightness to camera distance from the mapped river polyline so walking a patrol toward the stream brings it up — strong sense-of-place payoff.
techniques.webAudioMapping: RIVER bed: shared noise buffer → bandpass (center ~1.0-1.5 kHz, Q~0.4) → slow LFO (0.05-0.1 Hz) on the bandpass .frequency (±300 Hz) for the breathing → riverGain (set by distance-to-river from the pure layer) → reverb send. River burbles: low-rate Poisson grains = 80-160 Hz sine 'plinks' through a bandpass, panned at the river position. RAIN bed: noise → lowpass ~ shaped by intensity, gain = weather.precip?level:0, ducks birds. Rain droplets (only when close/under cover): Poisson short highpassed noise ticks (reuse the 'impact' recipe family). All grain schedules are the deterministic Poisson-from-hash from technique 6. River position can come from terrain (the river-aware planner already knows the channel); distance→gain via the same camera-distance math spatial() already computes.
techniques.source: Audiokinetic 'Generating Rain With Pure Synthesis' (noise bed + synthesized droplets, randomized density/pitch); binaura.net WebPd rain/wind experiment (continuous HP-filtered noise wind + ADSR droplet rain)

techniques.name: Anthrophony of place: generator hum (additive harmonics) + scheduled adhan + COP/village emitters
techniques.howItWorks: The signature of THIS setting is anthrophony: the ever-present diesel generator drone at the COP, the five-times-daily call to prayer drifting up from villages, distant dogs. The generator is additive synthesis — a low fundamental plus odd/even harmonics with a slow amplitude wobble (the engine 'lope') — proven for mains/engine hum. The adhan is a scheduled, NON-random event (it happens at fixed prayer times tied to solarLight/clock, which is doctrinally and emotionally right — it marks time, and a firefight that interrupts it lands hard), synthesized as filtered formant tones (a melismatic vocal line is faked with a sawtooth through vowel-formant peaking filters, heavily lowpassed and reverbed for the distance-across-the-valley quality). These anchor the COP and villages as REAL places and are the single biggest 'sense of place' lever the genre has.
techniques.webAudioMapping: GENERATOR: persistent voice = OscillatorNode sine @ ~55-65 Hz (fundamental) + 3-5 harmonics (sawtooth or summed sines at 2f,3f,4f, decreasing gain) → lowpass 250 Hz → generatorGain panned/attenuated by camera distance to COP. 'Lope' = a 3-7 Hz LFO at low depth on a gain in the chain. ADHAN: pure layer fires a spot cue at fixed secondsOfDay marks (dawn/noon/etc., derived from solarLight thresholds — deterministic); synth recipe = 2-3 OscillatorNodes (sawtooth) through peaking formant filters (~700/1200/2600 Hz, vowel-like), with a slow programmed pitch contour (setValueCurveAtTime for the melisma), then lowpass ~1.5 kHz + heavy reverb-send for cross-valley distance, panned to the nearest village pos. Dogs/voices via the technique-6 Poisson scheduler. Generator only audible inside ~COP radius (distance gate in spatial()).
techniques.source: meettechniek.info additive synthesis (harmonic stacks); mynoise 50/60Hz hum generator (fundamental+harmonics model); setting reference: Sebastian Junger 'War' / Restrepo / The Outpost (generator, adhan, dogs as the COP soundscape)

techniques.name: The 'readable silence' contract: a calm-before floor that the combat layer ducks, and that surges quiet on a TIC
techniques.howItWorks: The project's stated soul is 'the readable silence of the calm-before' — so the ambient bed must DROP OUT (not fight) when combat starts, mirroring how STALKER uses sudden silence before a blowout to spike tension. The bed runs at a low, restrained floor; on the TIC rising edge (the existing inContact latch / tic_sting), duck the whole ambient bus hard and fast so the firefight reads against near-silence + the existing low drone, then SLOWLY restore the bed as contact decays — the exhale after the fight. This makes the ambience an active dramatic instrument rather than wallpaper, and directly serves the 'somber, not arcade-y' tone. It also naturally solves CPU/clarity: fewer ambient voices compete during the loudest moments.
techniques.webAudioMapping: Route ALL ambient voices into a single ambientBus GainNode → master (separate from the combat per-cue chains). The existing AudioFlags.inContact already gates the engine; on inContact rising edge call ambientBus.gain.setTargetAtTime(0.15, now, 0.4) (fast duck) and on falling edge setTargetAtTime(1.0, now, 12.0) (slow exhale, ~12 s). This reuses the exact pattern the tic_sting/radio duck already implies. The pure ambient-state layer can also lower biophony density toward zero while inContact (birds go quiet when shooting starts — true to life). Keep the generator/wind floor slightly present so it's silence-with-texture, not a dead mute.
techniques.source: STALKER sound design — silence-before-blowout tension (mordiomusic.com); project CLAUDE.md 'readable silence of the calm-before'; existing TIC one-way speed latch + tic_sting (lib/audio/synth.ts)

keyInsights: The ambient bed is a CONTINUOUS STATE, not discrete events — so it needs a NEW pure module (ambient-state.ts, sibling of the existing mapper.ts) that maps sim signals → target gains/params, and a NEW render module owning a PERSISTENT voice bank that chases those targets via setTargetAtTime. Do not bolt it onto the one-shot cue pipeline; run it as a parallel ambientBus so MAX_VOICES (combat) never starves the bed.

Every signal the bed needs ALREADY EXISTS deterministically on World: solarLight() (0..1 smooth dawn/dusk), windVector() (diurnal anabatic/katabatic + synoptic), state.weather (label/wind/windDir/precip/visibilityM), secondsOfDay/day, and COP/village/river positions. The pure ambient layer is a function of these — zero new sim state, zero determinism risk, and it auto-syncs with the on-screen night-light/weather render.

Two universal anti-repetition laws do the heavy lifting: (1) unsynchronized, mutually-irrational loop/LFO periods so the combined bed effectively never repeats; (2) detailed sounds (birds, dogs, gusts, adhan) live as Poisson-scheduled SPOT one-shots, NOT baked into loops. Determinism is preserved by deriving every arrival time + pitch + pan from a pure hash (RNG.hashString) of (layer, time-bucket, index) — the same cueVar trick already in cue.ts.

Krause's acoustic-niche hypothesis is the mix-mud cure: pre-assign each layer a reserved frequency band (generator <250 Hz, wind howl 100-400 Hz / whistle 1-3 kHz, river 0.4-6 kHz notched at 3-4 kHz, birds 2-5 kHz, insects 4-7 kHz, voices/adhan 0.3-2 kHz) and band-limit it there. Separation by design, not by runtime EQ fighting — and it keeps the bed legible under the combat layer.

Two big sense-of-place wins are nearly free in Web Audio: convolution reverb from a procedurally-generated exp-decay noise IR (the canyon roll of a distant report, NO sample shipped) on a parallel wet send; and anthrophony — additive generator hum + scheduled adhan + village dogs — which is THIS setting's signature and the strongest 'real place' lever the genre has.

The bed must be a dramatic instrument, not wallpaper: it runs at a restrained floor and DUCKS HARD on the inContact rising edge (fast, ~0.4s) then exhales slowly (~12s) — serving the project's literal 'readable silence of the calm-before' soul and reusing the existing TIC latch. Restraint is the brief; an always-loud bed would be the arcade-y failure mode to avoid.
pitfalls: MIX MUD: stacking broadband noise layers (wind + river + rain) without frequency partitioning turns the bed to grey hiss. Band-limit each layer to its acoustic niche and notch the bed where a foreground layer (birds, adhan) lives. Do NOT rely on a master compressor to fix overlap — it pumps and flattens dynamics.

DETERMINISM BREAK: any wall-clock or Math.random in the cue/state-mapping layer violates Law 7. The pure ambient-state module must derive ALL variation (Poisson arrivals, pitch, pan) from RNG.hashString of (layer, time-bucket, index). Math.random() is allowed ONLY inside render-side noise-buffer fill (as the existing synth.ts already scopes it).

ARCADE-Y / TOO-LOUD: an ever-present, full-volume nature bed reads as a theme-park ride, not a somber COP. Keep the floor restrained, let silence breathe (Splice: constant loudness fatigues), and duck hard for combat. The reference is the readable quiet of Restrepo, not a soundscape app.

AUDIBLE LOOP SEAM: synchronized loop/LFO periods (or two layers restarting in phase) make the ear lock onto the repeat. Use mutually-irrational rates and independent start phases; never share a period across two beds.

VOICE-POOL STARVATION & LEAKS: the combat path tears down voices via setTimeout and caps at MAX_VOICES=24. Persistent bed voices must live OUTSIDE that pool (built once at unlock, never auto-torn-down) or they'll be culled mid-fight or leak nodes. Crossfade transitions with AudioParam ramps only — never source.start/stop on a weather/time change (that clicks and reallocates).

PERF: do NOT instantiate the full Farnell 10-50 bandpass bank, nor regenerate the reverb IR per frame. 3-5 parallel biquads approximate the wind bank fine; regenerate the convolver IR only on weather.label change (infrequent, offline render). One shared noise buffer feeds all noise layers (the codebase already does this with _noise).

PAUSE/WARP GATE: the bed must obey the same gate as cues — silent (or frozen) on pause/warp, and it must not dump a backlog or restart on resume. The existing tick() skip()/gate logic is the template; ambient gains should ramp to 0 on pause, not hard-stop.

CLICKS ON PARAM JUMPS: stepping any gain/cutoff (especially the combat duck and weather crossfade) clicks. Always use setTargetAtTime / equal-power cos-sin ramps with an appropriate time-constant (fast ~0.15-0.4s for ducks, slow ~8-12s for weather/time-of-day).
